newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India ONGC gas output falls amid pipeline work.
newsitem.headline: India ONGC gas output falls amid pipeline work.

text.p: India's state Oil and Natural Gas Corp Ltd's monthly gas production from the Bombay offshore basin fell in January due to a shutdown of the platform, a company official said on tuesday.
"There was an intentional 23 day shutdown to connect the South Basin-Hazira pipeline," he said, explaining the fall in ONGC's January gas production.
The connection involved connecting a platform to the pipline.
The gas pipeline consists of two lines, each 20 million cubic metres per day capacity. Only the first line is being utilised with the second in reserve for future upgrading.

Natural gas production from the Basin, ONGC's main gas producing area, fell in January to 917.4 million cubic metres from 1.1652 trillion cubic metres in December and from 1.2018 trillion cubic metres a year earlier.
Liquid petroleum gas (LPG) production was also affected by the shutdown, falling to 83,450 tonnes in January from 98,800 tonnes in December and compared with 101,070 tonnes year-on-year.

The crude output from the Bombay High field was not affected by the shutdown, but ONGC's crude production in January extended its fall amid continuing problems at Neelam, one of the major fields, the official said.
January's output from Bombay High fell to 1.644 million tonnes from 1.69 million tonnes in December and 1.862 million tonnes year-on-year.
Production from ONGC's remaining fields other than Bombay High, was steady at 45,000 tonnes compared with 46,000 tonnes in January last year.
